items.title: An Operating System for Shared Reality
items.summary: Frames Cyberdelic OS as an ethical interface between private apertures and a continuously negotiated shared reality.

items.title: Asynchronous Co-Presence
items.summary: Describes correspondence across distance and delay as a spacious creative presence with continuity, voice, and time to ferment.

items.title: A Village of Agents
items.summary: Replaces the singular AI oracle with an ecology of distinct, bounded agents whose offices, histories, and disagreements remain visible.

items.title: The Gathering Intelligence
items.summary: Imagines intelligence that holds a shared encounter, protects participant boundaries, and helps groups think without manufacturing consensus.

items.title: The Physics We Choose
items.summary: Treats interface rules as designed physics that shape attention, memory, status, ambiguity, and the kinds of consciousness a world cultivates.

items.title: First Light
items.summary: Positions the project as a situated signal toward a desirable future, open to correction, collaboration, and forms its author cannot build alone.

items.title: The Hearth: Intelligence Comes Home
items.summary: Makes local-first intelligence a moral architecture in which people govern private memory, models, permissions, energy, and every crossing to the cloud.

items.title: The Lived Interface
items.summary: Proposes a spatial interface of Home, Village, Field, Forest, Table, Observatory, and Press where relation becomes sensorially legible.

items.title: The Lensmaker: Portable Apertures
items.summary: Defines an authored lens as a calibrated and source-grounded pattern of attention that widens perception without impersonating its creator.

items.title: The Mirror Archive
items.summary: Turns selected conversational traces into a local, cited, and revisable proposal for self-recognition rather than a totalizing model of the person.

items.title: The Writing Table
items.summary: Designs a ritual for humans and distinct intelligences to attend independently, question one another, and preserve polyphony through structured deliberation.

items.title: Ports and Weather Stations
items.summary: Treats social platforms as algorithmic climates and proposes deliberate ports that preserve source, mediation, context, and the reason something was carried inward.

items.title: The Ledger, the Anchor, and the Inscription
items.summary: Separates revisable living memory, privately provable anchored memory, and rare public inscription so each can hold a different temperature.

items.title: The Open Anatomy
items.summary: Maps open technical organs for a local-first system while keeping Cyberdelic OS defined by constitutional boundaries instead of any replaceable tool.

items.title: The First Small World
items.summary: Reduces the operating-system vision to a testable prototype containing one home, Familiar, Lensmaker, table, correspondence, field, and memory ritual.

items.title: The Archipelago: Sovereign Worlds, Shared Sky
items.summary: Envisions independently governed Homes, Villages, and Cities joined by shared protocols, selective memory, bridges, and a non-sovereign public sky.

items.title: One World, Many Interfaces
items.summary: Keeps one semantic world continuous across spatial, voice, analytical, audiovisual, table, and plain-text interfaces selected for different modes of consciousness.

items.title: You Carry the Doorway
items.summary: Makes the phone a secure, offline-capable doorway into a sovereign home node, so life can enter the system without shrinking the Hearth into a mobile app.

items.title: A Medium for Becoming
items.summary: Imagines a restrained archive that reflects changing patterns of attention and identity without converting self-knowledge into prediction, optimization, or tasks.

items.title: Aperture Design as a Cultural Form
items.summary: Proposes aperture design as a creative discipline for carrying a versioned pattern of attention, with consent, sources, limits, and calibration made public.

items.title: Conversation Now, Cultivation Later
items.summary: Joins immediate voice conversation to bounded background cultivation governed by explicit limits on interruption, privacy, compute, agents, and duration.

items.title: The Chain Beneath the Village
items.summary: Places blockchain beneath daily life as a notary, treasury, and court for selected proofs, civic state, and cultural permanence rather than ordinary activity.

items.title: A Civic Economy Without Speculative Land
items.summary: Builds an economy around genuinely scarce care, trust, compute, and stewardship while separating money, standing, and governance.

items.title: The Game of Shared Understanding
items.summary: Makes collective attention the engine of an ecological world where depth, plurality, stewardship, creation, and relation visibly develop the landscape.

items.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs
items.summary: Turns ideological difference into expeditions and public weather that can yield bridges, crux maps, contested timelines, and durable shapes without forced consensus.

items.title: Creation Alters the Geography
items.summary: Makes original creation the deepest participation loop, where people and agents gather around a dark region and produce work that changes the shared world.

items.title: Vocations, Not Classes
items.summary: Defines roles as offices of attention whose tools arise from accepted constraints, demonstrated practice, contextual trust, and plural identity.

items.title: The World Is the Interface
items.summary: Centers head-up computing on embodied life, authored relation to place, nonhuman apertures, and a loop that repeatedly returns attention to the physical world.
